column3: “With partiality” is rendered “with an attitude of personal favoritism”; “the Lord of glory” is rendered “our glorious Lord.”
“Splendid apparel” is rendered “fine clothes,” and “shabby” “dirty.”
“Look upon” is rendered “pay special attention to,” and “honorably” “in a good place”; NASB follows the critical text (“or sit down,” without “here”).
“Thoughts” is rendered “motives.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the poor of this world”); “brothers” is rendered “brethren.”
NASB adds “personally.”
“Denigrating” is rendered “blaspheme,” and “good” “fair”; “called upon you” is rendered “by which you have been called.”
“Keep” is rendered “are fulfilling.”
Close to the Greek.

NASB follows the critical text (“do not commit … do commit”).
“Freedom” is rendered “liberty”; NASB supplies “those who.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “and”; “without mercy” is rendered “merciless.”
“Profit” is rendered “use,” and “the faith” “that faith.”
NASB follows the critical text, without the Textus Receptus “now.”
NASB supplies “that”; “the needful things” is rendered “what is necessary.”
NASB adds “being.”
NASB follows the critical text (“without the works”); “will say” is rendered “may well say.”
“Well you are doing” is rendered “You do well.”
NASB follows the critical text (“useless”; the Textus Receptus has “dead”); “O foolish man” is rendered “you foolish fellow.”
NASB adds “when.”
“By the works” is rendered “as a result of the works.”
“Counted” is rendered “reckoned”; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text, without “therefore.”
